newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Monti points to low implementation of procurement.
newsitem.headline: Monti points to low implementation of procurement.

text.p: The European Commission will address EU member states' failure to implement the EU's 11 public procurement directives in a forthcoming green paper, Commissioner Mario Monti said on Friday.
Monti said in a speech there were still 17 cases in which national measures to implement the directives have not been taken, even though some deadlines expired several years ago.

In total 39 legal procedures have been opened against the member states, he said in the speech to Orgalime -- linking the EU and 25 trade federations in the mechanical, electrical, electronic, and metal working industries of 16 European countries.
"Poor implementation is only one of several issues regarding public procurement," he said of the forthcoming paper.
Monti told the meeting the EU's public authorities spend about 720 billion Ecus every year to buy goods and services, representing 11 percent of EU gross domestic product.

Orgalime Secretary General Patrick Knox-Peebles said that the failure of member states to transpose the directives had produced extra burdens for companies exporting from one EU member state to another.
He said small and medium-sized companies are discouraged by the complexity of public procurement rules.
